entries.test: Whether the guardrailed Bing chatbot of late February 2023 could be prompted to produce publishable misinformation, as shown in Marcus's example and independent reproductions such as Rathi's.
entries.note: Marcus withheld the prompt, so the evidence comes from his screenshot and from others who reproduced it.

entries.test: Whether documented high-volume AI-generated misinformation campaigns, for example in platform or AI-lab threat reports, became a recognised problem after March 2023.
entries.note: The surrounding text is about AI, which supports the 'generated with AI' framing. The claim is vague, but a plain reading exists.

entries.test: Whether there was a large, widely reported surge of generative-AI misinformation in the period shortly after March 2023, for example around 2023–2024.
entries.note: 'Soon', written in 2023, has lapsed by the evaluation date. 'Massive mess' is loose, but most readers would read it as a widely reported surge.

entries.test: Whether the OpenCage phone-lookup and Hangzhou number-plate rumour incidents involving ChatGPT occurred and caused harm, as documented by AIAAIC and the press.
entries.note: The 'tip of the iceberg' part is an extrapolation that is hard to grade. The two incidents themselves can be checked.

entries.test: Soumil Rathi's 1 March 2023 tweet showing Bing producing misinformation from a single jailbreak prompt with no prior context.
entries.note: Marcus himself hedges the replication as only 'largely' successful (footnote 1).
'Imagine what... might do' does not commit to troll farms doing 'far worse'; the normalised version is firmer than his words.
